The claims check out against the passages:

- E = sum_i E_i is stated in W2025444507#003.
- Each E_i comes from an atomic subnet fed a descriptor of the local environment, such as symmetry functions or an AEV. W2025444507#003 covers symmetry functions, W2541404351#007 covers the AEV, and W4312043350#015 covers local atom-centered descriptors.
- Identical structure and weights across subnets, which keeps the energy invariant when two atoms are interchanged, is in W2025444507#003. That passage says the subnets are "constrained to be identical" for "invariance ... with respect to the interchanging of two atoms". It says "all subnets", with no mention of atom type, and the answer adds "for atoms of the same type". W2541404351#007 and W4312043350#015 do describe one network per element, and W2025444507#003 mentions "even if the two atoms are of the same type
